target.title: [Bug]: channels status --deep falsely reports not-running for an auto-loaded (no plugins.allow) channel plugin
target.body:
### Bug type

Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

### Beta release blocker

No

### Summary

openclaw channels status --deep reports a channel plugin as not-running (and plugins list may render it disabled) when the plugin is loaded via auto-load (no plugins.allow entry), even though the plugin is actually running — confirmed by gateway logs (provider started), live WebSocket message flow, and platform-side onlineStatus: online.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install a channel plugin whose manifest has activation: { onStartup: false, onChannels: ["<channel>"] }.
2. In openclaw.json, configure both plugins.entries.<id> and channels.<id>, but do NOT add a plugins.allow entry.
3. Restart the gateway; confirm the plugin actually runs — gateway log shows [<id>] provider started, platform shows the agent online, and a consumer message is auto-answered end-to-end.
4. Run `openclaw channels status --deep` → it reports not-running.

### Expected behavior

channels status --deep reports health: running when the plugin is loaded and the channel is active, regardless of whether it was loaded via auto-load or an explicit plugins.allow entry.

### Actual behavior

channels status --deep reports the channel as not-running (plugins list may render it disabled), while the gateway log shows [<id>] provider started, real-time WS messages flow (typing, inbound, acks), platform shows onlineStatus: online, and end-to-end message handling works.

### OpenClaw version

2026.7.1 (Gateway 2026.7.1)

### Operating system

Windows 11

### Install method

npm global (openclaw CLI); plugin installed via `openclaw plugins install <npm package>`

### Model

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO — display-layer defect in channels status / plugins list; no model is involved.

### Provider / routing chain

NOT_ENOUGH_INFO — defect is in the channels status / plugins list display logic, not the model/provider chain. For context only: the plugin connects to an external service (ClawRent) over WebSocket as a channel provider.

### Additional provider/model setup details

N/A — no model or provider chain is involved; the defect is in status display.

### Logs

```shell
# Gateway log (plugin actually running):
[clawrent] provider started (agentId=auto autoApprove=true)
[clawrent] session new: 019f72cc-...
[clawrent] onMessage type=dialogue.message
[clawrent] replied (93 chars)
[clawrent] runChannelInboundEvent done
[clawrent] onMessage type=system.message_ack

# Yet, in the same run:
$ openclaw channels status --deep
clawrent clawrent-provider: health:not-running

# Platform-side state contradicts the status output:
onlineStatus: "online"
providerProfile.status: "active"
```

### Screenshots, recordings, and evidence

The gateway log and platform onlineStatus above directly contradict the `not-running` status output. All real-runtime signals (provider started, WS message flow, end-to-end auto-answer, platform online) confirm the channel is running.

### Impact and severity

Affected: any user or operator running an auto-loaded channel plugin who inspects status via channels status --deep / plugins list.
Severity: Low–Medium — diagnostic/usability defect only (no functional break; the plugin works), but it reliably causes false "the plugin is broken" conclusions and wasted debugging.
Frequency: Always in auto-load mode (no plugins.allow) — observed on every channels status --deep run while the plugin remained actually running.
Consequence: users and maintainers treat a working plugin as broken; trust in channels status / plugins list is eroded.

### Additional information

Adding plugins.allow: ["<id>"] is NOT a workaround — in testing it switched the load path to a stricter mode that prevented registerFull from executing, so the plugin then genuinely did not start. The only working configuration is auto-load (no allow), under which channels status misreports.
Workaround: judge whether the plugin is running from the gateway log ([<id>] provider started) and the platform-side online status; ignore channels status --deep / plugins list output in auto-load mode.
Not classified as a cross-version regression — only OpenClaw 2026.7.1 was tested.
Suggested fix (hypothesis): the channels status --deep / plugins list display logic should reflect the actual loaded/runtime state regardless of whether the plugin was loaded via auto-load or an explicit plugins.allow entry. Either fix the display, or document that status output is unreliable in auto-load mode.
